endpoints.summary: Upload or replace a film's poster, streamed to private object storage

headers.Content-Length: integer, 1..2097152 bytes, REQUIRED - checked at the header, before the body is read. This check does NOT mean the body is never buffered: steps 6 and 7 of P-ADM-03 decode the image and measure its pixel dimensions, which needs the bytes. What the check buys is that the buffer's size is known and refused before a byte is read, so no request makes the process hold more than 2 MB (P-ADM-03)

body.file: one file part, image/jpeg or image/png or image/webp, magic bytes must match the declared type, must decode, 200..4000 by 300..6000 pixels, required
body.version: integer, the film's current version, REQUIRED. A second form part of the same multipart body - not a header and not a query parameter. Checked before any byte is streamed to S3, so a stale upload costs no object and leaves no orphan (P-ADM-12)

A NON-retryable S3 refusal - the credential is not permitted to write, the bucket does not exist, or a quota or policy refuses the object - is 500 INTERNAL_ERROR instead, because 'try again in a moment' is false for it and the admin cannot fix a storage credential from a form (P-ADM-03 exceptions 12 and 12b)

The previous object is never deleted (FR-ADR-012), so an audit row's before value still resolves to a real image. A deliberate replacement therefore costs storage and is otherwise harmless.

body.movie_id: integer, must exist, required. The film need not be published
body.screen_id: integer, must exist and be in service, required
body.starts_at: string, ISO-8601 local date and time in Asia/Kolkata, required. NAIVE LOCAL ONLY - a value carrying a Z, a +hh:mm offset or a zone name is 422 VALIDATION_FAILED and is never coerced (P-ADM-04, P-ADM-07)

body.base_price_paise: integer, 1 or more, required. Paise only; a decimal is rejected, never rounded. UPPER BOUND, and it is arithmetic and not a business figure: base_price_paise * (10000 + highest stored uplift_basis_points) + 5000 must be <= 2^63 - 1, so that FR-ADR-038's seat-price formula cannot overflow the bigint columns it runs in. At the highest seeded uplift of 3333 basis points that caps the base price at 691770197019033 paise. Above it, 422 VALIDATION_FAILED with P-ADM-10 exception 4's sentence. NO BUSINESS CEILING EXISTS in any source and none is invented - PROPOSED-PRICEBOUND-01 in the Lane notes
body.format_id: integer, must be an active row of the format vocabulary (P-ADM-23), optional. A showtime with no format answers null on the browse surface and is excluded by any format filter

400.description: The body does not parse, or it carries a property this endpoint does not define. Unknown properties are REJECTED and never ignored (P-ADM-01, the uniform rule at the head of S4)

201.description: The created showtime. The two times come back in the SAME naive local form they were sent in - Asia/Kolkata, no Z and no offset - not as UTC instants, so the form that submitted them can refill from the response without converting (the rule at the head of S4). This block said ISO-8601 instant in UTC and that was the defect

endpoints.summary: Return the full seat layout and objective seat states for one showtime

200.description: The complete map. Never paginated, never partial. Cache-Control: no-store, because the client polls it every 3 seconds.

body.screen: {id, name, rows, cols}. rows and cols are DERIVED per response as max(gr) and max(gc) over THIS SHOWTIME's seat set, never over the screen's current seats and never from a stored column — no screen row carries them (EP-ADM-16 accepts only cinema_id and name). Taking the maximum over the current seats would let a seat added after this showtime was created widen this showtime's extent, which moves P-BRW-16's band rules and therefore misstates seat category for a customer who does not perceive colour (P-BRW-08, P-BRW-10, P-ADM-14).
body.categories: array of {id, name, price_paise} — already rounded by FR-ADR-038's rule. Ordered by the lowest gr at which the category appears in THIS SHOWTIME'S SEAT SET, ascending, with id ascending as the tiebreak, so the legend reads in the order the bands are drawn and the client never sorts (P-BRW-16). A category with no seat in this showtime's seat set is not returned. Scoped to the seat set and never to the screen's current seats, exactly as seats, rows and cols already are (P-ADM-14): the two sets genuinely differ once a seat is added to or retired from the hall, and a category present on the screen but absent from this showtime could otherwise order a legend row for a band the map does not draw.
body.seats: array of {id, row, num, gr, gc, cat, price_paise, state, is_active} — this showtime's seat set as materialised at showtime creation (P-ADM-14), never the screen's current seats — ordered by gr ASC then gc ASC; state is one of available|held|sold; price_paise is this seat's own already-rounded integer price, equal to its category's, so the client sums integers and performs no rounding of its own (P-BRW-10, FR-ADR-038, FR-ADR-045); is_active is a required boolean, false for a seat retired after this showtime was created, which is returned and drawn but is never selectable and still carries its true state — is_active is not a fifth state and the state enum stays three values wide (P-BRW-08 exception 3, P-BRW-09, P-ADM-15). Every seat sharing a gr carries the same row string, which is the label the gutter renders (P-BRW-16).
body.poll_interval_seconds: integer, the value of SEATMAP_POLL_INTERVAL_SECONDS, default 3. Server configuration validated at boot (S7.9 cross-check 10) and published here so the client holds no constant of its own and one value governs (P-BRW-11). The server publishes the interval and does not police it; a client polling faster meets the rate limiter and nothing else.
body.max_seats_per_booking: integer, the value of MAX_SEATS_PER_BOOKING, default 10. Server configuration published here, exactly as poll_interval_seconds is, so the seat map's cap note (`Up to 10 seats.`) and its local eleventh-tap refusal render the server's figure and the client ships no literal of its own (S-SEA-09, CR-002 C-1, approved SRC-008 NIGHT-1). The hold endpoint stays the enforcement point (P-HLD-04).

endpoints.summary: Release one seat from a live hold, keeping the rest

path_params.hold_token: string, opaque, exactly 43 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet, required
path_params.seat_id: integer, positive, must be a member of this hold's seat set

200.description: The seat was released. The remaining hold is returned with its unchanged expires_at. An empty seats array means the hold has ended. P-HLD-08's eight numbered steps are the procedure and the block does not repeat them; two are easy to miss and neither is optional - step 6 DEL cache:seatmap:{showtime_id} AFTER the lock release, and step 8, which on the LAST seat also removes the token from holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id} so P-HLD-04's cap stops counting a hold that has ended.

body.expires_at: string, ISO-8601 instant in UTC, unchanged
body.seats: array of {seat_id: integer, label: string, category: string, price_paise: integer}

403.description: The token belongs to another user.

409.description: The hold has already expired. A confirm in flight for the same hold does not refuse the release: the ordering settles it, per P-HLD-08.

This is the only 422 on this endpoint and it never covers a malformed token - a token of the wrong shape is 400 REQUEST_INVALID, one step earlier, because request framing is checked before the hold is read.

endpoints.authorisation_rule: The router dependency admits any authenticated principal holding an existing user row - no role is excluded; the handler asserts the hold record's user_id equals the caller's before the compare-and-delete script runs, and the script itself compares the hold's token so a lock this hold does not own can never be deleted.

endpoints.summary: Release an entire hold

path_params.hold_token: string, opaque, exactly 43 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet, required

204.description: The whole hold was released. P-HLD-08 carries the numbered procedure and it is SEVEN steps, not one: assert the caller owns the hold; compare-and-delete every key in ascending seat_id order; remove those keys from instance:{instance_id}:holds; delete the hold record; REMOVE THE TOKEN FROM holds:user:{user_id}:showtime:{showtime_id}, without which P-HLD-04's cap keeps counting a hold that no longer exists and the customer cannot re-take the seats they just gave back; DEL cache:seatmap:{showtime_id} AFTER the releases and never before, without which the seats read held to everyone else for up to the cache TTL instead of about three seconds; then answer 204 with no body. Steps 2 to 6 are best-effort - every structure carries the hold's TTL - and a compare-and-delete returning 0 for one seat is not an error and does not stop the loop.

400.description: The hold token is malformed - not exactly 43 characters, or carrying a character outside the URL-safe base64 alphabet. Checked before Redis is touched. REQUEST_INVALID, never HOLD_EXPIRED, for the reason given on EP-HLD-02.

403.description: The token belongs to another user.

409.description: The hold has already expired. None of the release steps run: there are no keys to release, and the hold record and the index entry carried the same TTL and are gone with them. In particular NO cache:seatmap DEL runs on this branch - an expiry frees seats without telling the cache anywhere in this document, and adding one here would invent an invalidation the expiry path has never had (P-HLD-02 exception 3). A confirm in flight for the same hold does not refuse the release: the ordering settles it, per P-HLD-08.

429.description: The per-user or per-IP token bucket is empty.

503.description: Redis is unreachable.

Nothing is released twice; the compare-and-delete script is a no-op against a key that is gone or that carries another token.

endpoints.summary: Confirm a held selection into a booking, capturing the simulated payment first

headers.Idempotency-Key: string, 1..255, REQUIRED — a missing header is 400 REQUEST_INVALID. GENERATED BY THE CLIENT, never by the server: crypto.randomUUID()'s canonical 36-character form, 122 random bits from a CSPRNG, one per CONFIRM ATTEMPT (not one per hold). It is written to sessionStorage before the request is sent and re-sent unchanged on any repeat of the same attempt, including one whose outcome the client never learned. A fresh key is minted only when there is no stored key, when the stored key was minted against a different hold_token, or when the previous attempt returned 402 PAYMENT_FAILED — the one outcome specified to have committed nothing (P-PAY-09)

body.hold_token: string, opaque, exactly 43 characters from the URL-safe base64 alphabet, required
body.showtime_id: integer, positive, required, must match the showtime the hold was taken on

201.description: The booking was created. The simulated payment reached captured before the booking row was inserted.

body.booking_reference: string, the PRESENTATION FORM FR-XXXX-XXXX including its hyphens - the same shape EP-TKT-01 and every other endpoint returning a reference carries. It is re-formatted at serialisation from the 8 characters stored on the booking row; the 8-character stored form is never what crosses the wire (P-TKT-01)
body.starts_at: string, ISO-8601 instant serialised WITH THE CINEMA'S UTC OFFSET taken from the cinema row, e.g. 2026-08-20T14:00:00+05:30 - never UTC, never a hardcoded offset. The client renders the wall-clock part as given and CONVERTS NOTHING (P-BRW-06, FR-ADR-018, P-ADM-26)
body.seats: array of objects: {seat_id, seat_label, seat_category_name, price_paise, base_price_paise_applied, uplift_basis_points_applied}
body.total_paise: integer, the sum of the already-rounded per-seat prices, never itself rounded
body.created_at: string, ISO-8601 instant serialised with the cinema's UTC offset, exactly as starts_at - it is shown to the customer as the time they booked, so it is a wall-clock instant and the client converts nothing

400.description: The Idempotency-Key header is missing or malformed, a required body field is missing, or the body carries a property this endpoint does not define.

401.description: No valid token. A guest cannot reach this endpoint.

402.description: The simulated provider returned failed. The transaction rolled back in full, taking its idempotency record with it, so nothing was booked and nothing was captured. The hold is untouched by this endpoint and survives if it has not expired. The published message makes no claim about which, because the confirm re-validates the hold at step 2 and the capture is step 6 and Redis is not read again before commit — it names what the server knows and points the customer at the countdown for the rest (P-PAY-01 exception 4). This is the only response after which the client mints a fresh Idempotency-Key.

403.description: The hold token exists but was issued to a different user.

409.description: The hold has expired, one or more seats were taken by another customer, or the same idempotency key is still in flight.

422.description: The same idempotency key was sent with a different request fingerprint.

429.description: Over the token bucket. Carries Retry-After in seconds.

500.description: Unhandled. The transaction rolled back and the request id is returned to the customer.

503.description: Redis is unreachable. The confirm path never falls back to PostgreSQL for the hold check.

endpoints.errors_deliberately_absent: SALES_CLOSED is NOT in the array above and cannot be raised by this endpoint. The sales cut-off is enforced once, at hold acquisition (P-HLD-06), and never re-checked at confirm - SRC-003 OPEN-BOOK-03 rules that anyone already holding seats may finish checking out, and a client ruling outranks FR-ADR-029 step 4, which reads otherwise (see this lane's contradiction 1). A customer whose cut-off passes mid-checkout completes normally: P-PAY-10 step 4 reads the showtime and does not gate on it. The absence is therefore a decision, not an omission, and it is recorded here because four sections discuss the cut-off at confirm and a reader who finds none of them conclusive would otherwise add the code.
endpoints.idempotency: Required. The record is inserted in Postgres in the same transaction, before any work, unique on (user_id, idempotency_key). A repeat with the same key and the same request fingerprint returns the winner's stored response body and status code when the winner is completed, and 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT with Retry-After while the winner is still running. A repeat with the same key and a different fingerprint is 422 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED. A key whose transaction rolled back is free to be used again. The record is never expired and never deleted. On 409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_FLIGHT the client re-sends the identical request automatically after Retry-After seconds, at most three times, and keeps its busy state while it does; every one of those re-sends spends a rate-limit token, which is why the count is bounded rather than a poll (P-PAY-09).
endpoints.rate_limit: Redis token bucket, two independent buckets and both must have a token: 10 per minute per user id, 30 per minute per real client IP. The real IP is the rightmost-but-one X-Forwarded-For entry with exactly one trusted proxy. The limiter fails closed with 503 when Redis is unreachable. A retry carrying an already-seen Idempotency-Key still consumes a token.
endpoints.authorisation_rule: The router requires a valid JWT for an existing user row and nothing more; the booking is always written against that user id, which is taken from the token and never from the request body. There is no role check beyond authentication, because no source restricts owning a booking by role and a guest is already stopped one step earlier at the hold.

query.screen_id: integer, positive, optional, narrows within the caller's resolved scope and never widens it. An out-of-service hall is a valid value: it stays in scope so its past figures stay readable (P-RPT-02, P-ADM-16).

200.description: The complete figures for the period. Never partial.

body.evaluated_at_utc: string, ISO-8601 instant taken from the injected clock
body.timezone: string, the cinema's IANA zone, Asia/Kolkata
body.scope_empty: boolean, true when the caller has no halls assigned

An empty array means one thing only: a manager with no assignment, whose response covers nothing (P-RPT-08). Consistent with EP-RPT-03, which carries all_halls plus the full screens array. SCR-RPT-01 renders its scope line and its hall filter from EP-RPT-03's screens array, looking these ids up in it, and never from this field alone — a screen fetching only this endpoint would render 'Halls shown: 3, 5.'

body.capacity: integer, the sum of seat_count_at_creation over the period's showtimes
body.occupancy_pct: number to one decimal place, or null when capacity is 0

When true the per-film sums are STRICTLY LESS THAN the headline figures and P-RPT-07's parts-equal-the-whole identity does not hold; the headline figures remain complete, because they are computed over every showtime in the period and are never summed from films. The role is not consulted: there is NO admin override and no manager override, so a caller holding the admin role reads their own bookings and nobody else's. No frozen source or approved record grants an admin the right to read an individual customer's booking; FR-ADR-009 makes admin a superset of manager and a manager is read-only reporting, and SRC-001 7.6's 'who booked this seat and when' is answered by the change log and the Phase 8 dashboard. E5's P-ACC-12 states that no v1 endpoint lets an admin read another customer's bookings, and this is that endpoint. This is deliberately not a customer-record lookup. Another account's booking returns the same 404 as a reference that does not exist. Applied once as a router dependency, never inside the handler.

endpoints.summary: Enqueue the receipt for this booking again

202.description: accepted; queued is false when nothing was enqueued, which is the case both when a dispatch was already in flight and when the first receipt has not been attempted yet

body.email_address: string, the account address the receipt will be sent to

404.description: the reference does not resolve for this caller

409.description: the booking's receipt_dispatch row is suppressed, which means it is a seeded demonstration booking whose address can never receive mail. Nothing was enqueued, nothing was changed and no rate-limit token was spent

429.description: one of three limiters refused, with Retry-After in seconds carrying whichever one it was: the per-booking resend interval gives 300 minus the elapsed seconds, which is 240 at 60 seconds elapsed and renders as 4 minutes; the per-user lookup bucket of 20 per minute gives 3; the per-IP lookup bucket of 60 per minute gives 1 and renders with the singular, and it is the one that refuses first behind a shared address

503.description: Redis is unreachable, so the rate limiter fails closed

endpoints.idempotency: A request against a suppressed row returns 409 RECEIPT_SUPPRESSED and changes nothing, on the first press and on every press after it; the state is terminal and no retry can move it. A request against a booking whose first receipt has not been attempted yet — receipt_dispatch is pending with attempts 0, which is the state a resend hits while the worker is down — enqueues nothing, changes nothing, spends no rate-limit token, and returns 202 with queued=false. A repeat while a dispatch is in flight (sending, or pending with attempts above 0) also enqueues nothing and returns 202 with queued=false. A repeat inside RECEIPT_RESEND_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS returns 429. A repeat after a completed or failed send increments dispatch_seq on the single receipt_dispatch row, sets it back to pending, and enqueues exactly one new outbox message with topic receipt.send, so a customer never receives two receipts from one press.
endpoints.rate_limit: per booking: one accepted resend per RECEIPT_RESEND_MIN_INTERVAL_SECONDS (ASSUMED starting value 300). Also the per-user booking-lookup bucket of 20 per minute (FR-ADR-058)
endpoints.authorisation_rule: The authenticated caller may resend only for a booking whose user_id equals their own user id. NO ROLE IS EXEMPT and there is no override parameter, for the same reason as EP-TKT-01: no frozen source or record grants an admin the right to act on an individual customer's booking, and this endpoint's 202 body carries the customer's email address, so an admin override here would be a customer-record read by another route. An admin who must answer for a receipt uses the change log and receipt_dispatch, which record what happened without disclosing the address. The reference is resolved through P-TKT-02, whose 404 is byte-identical for a malformed, unknown, and another-customer's reference, so this endpoint is not an enumeration oracle either.
